title: Agnostics: Learning to Synthesize Code in Any Programming Language with a Universal Reinforcement Learning Environment

Q1.quote: To evaluate Agnostics, we train and benchmark models on 5 low-resource programming languages.

Q2.quote: Using Agnostics, we train Qwen 3 4B and 8B on Ag-Codeforces-X specialized to Fortran, Julia, R, Lua, and OCaml.

Q3.quote: We use the AdamW optimizer (Loshchilov & Hutter, 2019) with a learning rate of 5 × 10−6 and a cosine decay schedule with a warmup of 0.1 epochs. We process 4 prompts in each batch, with group size 32 per prompt. When training we use temperature 0.7 and disable reasoning in hybrid models.

Q4.quote: We fine-tune Qwen 3 4B for 3 epochs (batch size 64, learning rate 2 × 10−5 , cosine learning rate decay with warmup ratio 0.1). [seule référence entraînée : la distillation ; les autres références sont des modèles publiés évalués tels quels]

Q5.quote: We provide references to our data, code, and artifacts at agnostics.abgru.me. [...] and our training framework at github.com/nuprl/agnostics-framework.

Q6.quote: We compared between GRPO group sizes of 16, 32 and 64 by training the same model on Lua. [...] As we found no significant difference between the temperature settings and between group sizes 32 and 64, we chose the smaller group size due to limited resources, and used the recommended temperature settings.
